unions.applicationFeeNotes: $75 Apprentice administration fee, paid yearly. Full membership has a one-time $1,600 initiation fee, less qualifying Apprentice credits and the initial Apprentice fee.
unions.description: National union of professional performers in English-language recorded media (outside BC, where UBCP/ACTRA is the autonomous branch). Represents actors, background performers, choreographers, dancers, singers, puppeteers, stunt coordinators and stunt performers.
unions.duesNotes: Full members: $195 basic annual dues plus 2.25% working dues on gross earnings, combined maximum $4,000 a year.

jurisdictions.notes: ACTRA Toronto and ACTRA Ottawa branches

unions.name: ACTRA

requirements.text: Check the "join ACTRA" box on a qualifying work permit; there is a 6-week window to join as an Apprentice
Pay the $75 Apprentice fee and complete the new-member orientation

Apprentice routes: graduate of an eligible acting program (apply within one year), a qualifying role on an ACTRA production, Additional Background Performer status, or a reciprocal agreement (e.g. Canadian Actors' Equity Association)
Additional Background Performer: 15 days of background work within a 12-month period

tiers.description: At least one qualifying work permit (principal, acting or stunt roles; background permits excluded), or a course of studies from an eligible school within the past year.
tiers.name: Apprentice

tiers.description: Three qualifying work permits and/or credits. No time limit while Apprentice membership is maintained.
tiers.name: Full Member

unions.name: UBCP/ACTRA

departments.description: The driving force behind the artistic and dramatic visualization of the script.
departments.name: Direction

roles.description: A Director is the driving force in the dramatic and artistic aspects of an audiovisual work. The Director visualizes and defines the style and structure of the script.
roles.name: Director

roles.description: Responsible for breaking down all elements presented in a script and maintaining the shooting schedule.
roles.name: 1st Assistant Director

departments.description: Ensuring narrative and visual consistency throughout the filming process.
departments.name: Script & Continuity

roles.description: The guardian of continuity, timing, and editing notes for the production. Tracks narrative logic across takes.
roles.name: Script Supervisor

departments.description: Administrative and logistical command for the production budget and operations.
departments.name: Production Office

roles.description: Oversees general operations and implementation of the production budget.
roles.name: Production Manager (PM)

roles.description: Manages office operations, travel, insurance, and vendor relations.
roles.name: Production Coordinator

departments.description: On-set management and communication bridge between creative and technical departments.
departments.name: Assistant Directors

roles.description: Creates daily call sheets and prep documentation, ensuring all required elements are reflected.
roles.name: Second Assistant Director (2AD)

roles.description: Assigned any and all necessary tasks by the senior ADs. Entry level position.
roles.name: Set PA (PA)

departments.description: Responsible for finding and securing environments for filming.
departments.name: Locations

roles.description: Responsible for finding filming locations, securing contracts, and operational needs.
roles.name: Location Manager (LM)

roles.description: Works on set to ensure permits are respected and that the location remains clean.
roles.name: Location Production Assistant (LPA)

departments.description: Visual generation of sets, environments, and overall design concepts.
departments.name: Art Dept

roles.description: Creative head responsible for visualization and generation of set design and overall concept.
roles.name: Production Designer (PD)

roles.description: Coordinates the preparation and execution of all visual elements in the Art Department.
roles.name: Art Director (ART)

departments.description: Dressing and detailing sets with furniture, decor, and textures.
departments.name: Set Decoration

roles.description: Creative lead responsible for the decor and interior/exterior dressing of all sets.
roles.name: Set Decorator

roles.description: Coordinates procurement and placement of decor elements as per the vision.
roles.name: Assistant Set Decorator

roles.description: Responsible for sourcing, purchasing, and renting furniture and decor items.
roles.name: Buyer

roles.description: Manages the set dressing crew in the physical layout and installation of decor.
roles.name: Lead Dresser

roles.description: Executes the physical dressing and arrangement of furniture on set.
roles.name: Set Dresser

roles.description: Maintains the decor during filming and handles continuity of dressing elements.
roles.name: On-Set Dresser

departments.description: Design, procurement, and maintenance of all on-screen character apparel.
departments.name: Costume Department

roles.description: Creative visionary for the look of all characters' wardrobe and accessories.
roles.name: Costume Designer

roles.description: Supports the Designer in sourcing, research, and department logistics.
roles.name: Assistant Costume Designer

roles.description: Administrative lead for the department, managing budget and inventory.
roles.name: Wardrobe Coordinator

roles.description: Supervises the on-set wardrobe crew and character wardrobe continuity.
roles.name: Key Wardrobe

roles.description: Responsible for the organization and maintenance of the wardrobe trailer.
roles.name: Truck Supervisor

roles.description: Highly skilled technician responsible for pattern making and structural construction.
roles.name: Cutter

roles.description: Responsible for garment construction, alterations, and maintenance.
roles.name: Sewer

roles.description: Assists cast members with costume changes and maintains character continuity.
roles.name: Dresser

departments.description: Personnel aesthetics, character design, and prosthetic applications.
departments.name: Hair & Makeup

roles.description: Department head for makeup, supervising artists and defining character looks.
roles.name: Key Makeup Artist

roles.description: Applies makeup to cast and background under the direction of the Key.
roles.name: Assistant Makeup

roles.description: Department head for hair, supervising stylists and character hair design.
roles.name: Key Hair

roles.description: Executes hair styling for cast and background as per the department vision.
roles.name: Assistant Hair

roles.description: Specialized artist for the application and maintenance of prosthetic effects.
roles.name: Prosthetics Artist

departments.description: Optics, lighting, and visual capture technical crew.
departments.name: Camera Department

roles.description: Chief of camera and lighting, responsible for the cinematic look.
roles.name: Director of Photography (DOP)

roles.description: Responsible for camera maintenance, focus pulling, and technical assembly.
roles.name: Assistant Camera (1st/2nd)

departments.description: Support equipment, camera movement, and lighting modification.
departments.name: Grip

roles.description: Supervises the grip crew and manages all support and movement equipment.
roles.name: Key Grip

roles.description: Administrative lead for the grip department, managing equipment and personnel.
roles.name: Best Boy Grip

roles.description: Specialized grip responsible for the operation and maintenance of the camera dolly.
roles.name: Dolly Grip

roles.description: Technician responsible for rigging support equipment and light modification.
roles.name: Grip

departments.description: Electrical distribution and lighting equipment management.
departments.name: Lighting/Electric

roles.description: Chief of the electrical department, executing the DOP's lighting plan.
roles.name: Gaffer

roles.description: Manages electrical equipment inventory and coordinates the electric crew.
roles.name: Best Boy Electric

roles.description: Responsible for the operation and safety of the production power generators.
roles.name: Generator Operator

roles.description: Technician responsible for the physical placement and operation of lighting fixtures.
roles.name: Lamp Operator

departments.description: The physical fabrication and scenic finishing of sets and props.
departments.name: Construction & Paint

roles.description: Manages the set construction budget, logistics, and personnel.
roles.name: Construction Coordinator

roles.description: Supervises the woodworking crew in set fabrication and assembly.
roles.name: Head Carpenter

roles.description: Fabricates sets and structural elements using wood and specialized materials.
roles.name: Carpenter

roles.description: Supervises the scenic painting crew and defines set finishing textures.
roles.name: Key Scenic Artist

roles.description: Applies specialized finishes and textures to sets to create realism.
roles.name: Scenic Painter

roles.description: Responsible for general set painting and finishing applications.
roles.name: Painter

departments.description: Post-production assembly of visual assets to create the final narrative.
departments.name: Picture Editing

roles.description: Creative head who works closely with the Director in crafting the final story.
roles.name: Picture Editor (PE)

roles.description: Works in the editing room, assisting with daily technical assemblies and organization.
roles.name: Assistant Picture Editor

departments.description: Post-production design and assembly of all auditory elements.
departments.name: Sound Editing

roles.description: Manages Post Sound elements including dialogue, ADR, SFX and Foley.
roles.name: Sound Editor (SE)

departments.description: Management of the finishing process after principal photography.
departments.name: Post Production

roles.description: Administrative liaison between Editorial and Producers.
roles.name: Post Production Supervisor (PPS)

roles.description: Assists Post Production Supervisors in all aspects of their duties.
roles.name: Post Production Coordinator (PPC)

departments.description: Financial management, payroll, and auditing for the production.
departments.name: Accounting Department

roles.description: Responsible for coordination, supervision and operation of the Accounting Department.
roles.name: Production Accountant

roles.description: Responsibilities include data entry, preparation of accounts payable, and payroll.
roles.name: Assistant Accountant

departments.description: Logistics and fleet management for cast, crew, and equipment.
departments.name: Transportation

roles.description: Responsible for movement of assets and personnel across locations.
roles.name: Coordinator / Driver

departments.description: Actors, stunt performers and background performers on camera.
departments.name: Performers

roles.description: Performs a speaking or principal role on camera.
roles.name: Actor

roles.description: Performs stunts and action sequences under the stunt coordinator's direction.
roles.name: Stunt Performer

roles.description: Appears on camera in non-speaking roles to populate scenes.
roles.name: Background Performer

departments.description: Screenwriters and story staff who write the script.
departments.name: Writing

roles.description: Writes the screenplay or teleplay for a film or series episode.
roles.name: Screenwriter

roles.description: Works with the writing team to develop, shape and revise scripts across a series.
roles.name: Story Editor

departments.description: Sourcing, building and managing every object actors handle on camera.
departments.name: Props

roles.description: Heads the props department, sourcing and managing all hand props and their continuity.
roles.name: Property Master

roles.description: Supports the property master on set and in prep, tracking props through each scene.
roles.name: Assistant Property Master

roles.description: Purchases and rents props to the property master's specifications.
roles.name: Props Buyer

departments.description: Recording dialogue and sound on set.
departments.name: Production Sound

roles.description: Records and mixes dialogue and on-set sound during filming.
roles.name: Production Sound Mixer

roles.description: Positions the boom microphone to capture dialogue without entering frame.
roles.name: Boom Operator

departments.description: Practical on-set effects such as rain, wind, smoke, fire and rigged gags.
departments.name: Special Effects

roles.description: Plans and runs practical effects safely, leading the special effects crew.
roles.name: Special Effects Coordinator

roles.description: Builds, rigs and operates practical effects under the coordinator.
roles.name: Special Effects Assistant

departments.description: Plants, trees, lawns and landscaping dressed on sets and locations.
departments.name: Greens

roles.description: Leads the greens department, designing and installing live and artificial greenery.
roles.name: Head Greensperson

roles.description: Installs, maintains and strikes greens on sets and locations.
roles.name: Greensperson

departments.description: On-set food service and medical coverage for cast and crew.
departments.name: Craft Service & First Aid

roles.description: Runs on-set snacks and refreshments for cast and crew throughout the shooting day.
roles.name: Head of Craft Service

roles.description: Provides on-set first aid and medical coverage; requires current first aid certification.
roles.name: First Aid Attendant

payRules.mealBreakNotes: Each meal period is 60 minutes and unpaid. If production calls a 30-minute catered first meal, it is paid work time. Under "Ontario Hours" the meal is paid.

payRules.mealBreakNotes: Meal breaks are unpaid. If production gives a 30-minute first meal instead, it is paid and counts as work time. Lunch is due within 6 hours (meal penalties after that).

payRules.notes: The daily fee is the minimum for a day. Overtime is 150% of your contracted hourly rate after 8 hours worked and 200% after 12, in 6-minute units.

payRules.mealBreakNotes: Meal period due by the end of the 6th hour; meal penalties are paid at the overtime rate in 0.1-hour units until it starts.
